title: drift-aware-multiobjective-canary-with-ethical-sampling
author: Ava Martinez
description: Context: As customers scale multi-tenant workloads, model rollouts must balance multiple objectives (latency, quality, fairness) while remaining sensitive to distributional drift and underrepresented cohorts. This PR introduces a new controller and supporting runtime primitives for a drift-aware, multi-objective canary that enforces stratified ("ethical") sampling so that small-but-critical cohorts are included during early validation. Motivation: Previous canary flows prioritized aggregate metrics and often missed regressions that only appeared in small slices; incidents in Q4 highlighted that missing these slices can cause downstream product regressions. Design summary: - Canary controller that runs staged traffic phases (shadow -> 1% -> 5% -> 25% -> 100%) with adaptive dwell times. - Per-cohort drift detectors compute a lightweight distributional distance (KS/JS proxy) and surface a cohort drift score. - Multi-objective gating: checks consider delta in model quality (task-level metric), latency p95, and cohort drift. Each gate evaluates a weighted objective; weights are configurable via rollout policy. - Ethical sampling layer: runtime sampler ensures that sampling for canary traffic is stratified by configured slice keys (e.g., locale, subscription_tier, device_type) with guaranteed minimum sample counts for rare slices. Sampling is implemented as a lightweight token tagging path integrated into request router. - Rollforward support: alongside automatic rollback triggers, controller supports controlled rollforward (increase step size) when confidence intervals tighten faster than expected. - Observability: new per-slice metrics exported to console and a dedicated rollout dashboard. Checklist: - [x] controller core and policy engine - [x] runtime sampler and token tagging - [x] cohort drift detector + lightweight aggregator - [x] unit and integration tests for gating logic - [x] e2e smoke tests against sample service - [x] rollout dashboard panels and alerts - [x] docs: runbook and operator guide Backwards compatibility: sampler integrates as an opt-in config on route-level rollout policies. Existing rollouts default to current behavior. If policy sets "stratified_sampling": true the new path is used. Testing and validation: unit tests for sampling determinism, integration tests for controller transitions, synthetic workload validation with injected drift, and a controlled canary against staging with representative cohorts. Rollout plan: staged deploy to dedicated clusters, enable in internal org for 48h with 1% traffic then 5% for 4h, run automated gating, then expand to 25% if all gates green, otherwise quarantine and snapshot traffic for replay and deeper evaluation. Rollback policy: automated rollback triggers if any of the following sustained for two consecutive windows (window = 5 minutes): - quality delta worse than configured threshold (default -2.0% relative) - latency p95 increase > 10% - cohort drift score > 0.25 for any configured slice - error rate spike > 0.2% For severe safety violations (e.g., hallucination-rate > threshold for NLU routes) controller will immediately cut traffic and snapshot requests for reproduction Monitoring and alerts: new alert rules added to console: rollout-gate-failure, cohort-drift-high, and ethical-sampler-imbalance. Migration notes: operators can toggle stratified_sampling per-route via the Console and the rollout policy API. Related work: builds on earlier gating controllers but extends to multi-objective scoring and sampling fairness. Linear items: ENG-1934 (controller core), PM-342 (product policy surface).
commits: feat(controller): add multi-objective canary controller and policy engine
feat(runtime): implement stratified token sampler and tag propagation
perf: batch cohort drift aggregation with streaming summarizer
test: add integration tests for gate evaluation and rollback triggers
docs: operator runbook, rollout dashboard panels and alerts
chore: telemetry schema updates and minor refactors
changes_summary: Adds a new canary controller that evaluates a configurable, weighted multi-objective score across quality, latency, and per-cohort drift, plus a runtime stratified sampler to include rare slices early in rollouts. Includes tests, metrics, dashboard panels, and operator docs.
review_thread: Rohit Patel: Nice overall design, two quick asks: (1) make drift threshold config per-cohort optional with sensible defaults, (2) document expected performance overhead of sampler on hot paths.

Ava Martinez: Addressed both in latest commits. Drift thresholds are policy-configurable and default to 0.2; added benchmarks and notes about sampler overhead (single-digit percent at 95th percentile) to perf/benchmarks and tagging.md.
Sofia Nguyen: Approved after seeing tests and dashboards. One nit: prefer clearer naming for "cohort drift score" in metrics (added suggestion: rollout.cohort_js_proxy).

Diego Alvarez: Left a request to add additional unit tests for extremely rare slice behavior (1 in 10k requests). Added integration test that synthesizes that distribution and validated sample guarantees.
release_notes: Introduce drift-aware multi-objective canary with optional stratified (ethical) sampling to ensure small cohorts are included in early rollouts; new rollout policy flags, dashboard panels, and operator runbook.
changelog_entry: Feature: drift-aware multi-objective canary + stratified sampling (ENG-1934).
rollout_policy_example:
name: stratified-canary
steps:
  - phase: shadow
    duration: 10m
  - phase: rollout
    traffic: 1%
    dwell: 2h
    stratified_sampling: true
    slices: ["locale", "subscription_tier"]
    weights: { quality: 0.6, latency: 0.25, drift: 0.15 }
operators_notes: When enabling on high-throughput routes, validate sampler metrics (telemetry/rollout.sampler.imbalance) and ensure policy weights reflect product tolerance for latency vs quality. For private deployments, confirm telemetry export is enabled so cohort aggregation works across nodes.
testing_and_validation: Unit + integration + synthetic drift tests included. Staging run executed with internal org; results attached in dashboard snapshot. Perf microbenchmarks show median sampler overhead < 1% and p95 overhead ~4% on large instances.
safety_considerations: Stratified sampling reduces the chance of missing rare-slice regressions but increases overall variance for aggregate metrics; gates use statistical tests with configurable confidence levels to avoid noisy rollbacks. Sensitive slices (PII-heavy routes) should remain opt-out until operator review.
notes_for_oncall: If a rollout triggers auto-rollback, the controller snapshots 1% of requests and stores tagged payloads to the incident bucket for replay. Use 'redwood rollout inspect' to retrieve snapshots. Look for spikes in rollout.gate_failure and cohort_drift_high alerts.
related_prs_and_docs: Related: ENG-17820 gating refactor PR; docs: docs/runbooks/rollout_guardrails.md.
